title: Jonvic: Plan to 'dramatize' VP Sara arrest prevented
summary: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of…

blocks.text: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of her in handcuffs and inside a detention facility. Duterte was issued with an arrest warrant by a Quezon City Regional Trial Court for a case of grave threats and Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the plan was to make it appear that the Vice President was being treated unfairly. “Ang drama nila gusto nila makulong siya, at naka-hand-cuff siya. The high drama na dapat makulong siya agad dito. (Their drama is that they want her behind bars and in handcuffs. The high drama that she should be jailed here (Camp Crame) right away,” said Remulla in a press briefing. “Hindi kami pumayag (We did not agree). We wanted to go according to the rules to the rues of law and to the rules of court and we accorded her the respect that her positions deserve,” she added. The Department of Justice filed charges of grave threats against Duterte in connection with the assassination threat she allegedly said in an online discussion with vloggers—threats directed to President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. On Friday, Sept. 4, the QC RTC Branch 98 issued an arrest warrant against her. The following day, Duterte arrived at the QC RTC to post bail. It was then that Durerte was quoted accusing the PNP of harassment, and remarked that she fear for her life and that she does not trust the court and the police. The truth according to the PNP Both Remulla and the Philippine National Police (PNP), through the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), denied the allegation of harassment and surveillance. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, CIDG director Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico narrated what actually happened the moment they received the arrest warrant from the Branch 98 of the QC RTC. He said the CIDG received the arrest warrant at 12:45 p.m. and immediately, a team from the unit’s Women and Children Protection Desk proceeded to Mandaluyong City where the Vice President is holding office to inform her camp of the court’s order. “We have coordinated with the Vice President Security Group because the subject of the warrant of arrest is the second highest official of the land and we know that there are security arrangements for the President and the Vice President,” said Morico. Morico said they have been in constant coordination with Duterte’s security officer in relation to the service of the arrest warrant and her camp, sent a certain Major Nabua to personally coordinate. The initial arrangement According to Morico, there were already negotiations between the CIDG and the Vice President Security Group since the issuance of the arrest warrant on Friday—and part of that coordination was the visit of the certain Major Nabua whom he said, interestingly asked where the Vice President would be detained inside Camp Crame. “I told him that there is still time for the Vice President to post bail because it’s a bailable offense, that we can escort her after all the booking procedures to the QC RTC to post bail,” said Morico. Morico said they were later told that the Vice President did not want to post bail. “But I was informed of the VSPG that she does not want to post bail. She wants to be incarcerated so they asked where is the jail facility,” said Morico. ‘I told the Major Nabua and his commanding officer that I will not commit the Vice President to jail facilities. She will be placed to conference room because we have to afford her the necessary respect due to her office,” he stressed. Of Jollibee and McDo Morico said they could not commit Duterte to any jail facility because they are full of notorious criminals and that the main detention facilities are undergoing renovation. The most that the CIDG could do, according to her, is to accommodate her to the CIDG conference room with some amenities that include a folding bed and the most expensive meal that the police could afford—from Jollibee and Mc Donald. “But we told them that they can bring food,” said Morico. Change of mind According to Morico, he said they waited until 1 a.m. the following day but did not show up. Instead, he said they were informed that the Vice President would go to QC Regional Trial Court instead to post bail. “So I dispatched a team to the house of the Vice President in San Juan to escort her. No need for armed unit because she has her own coming from the VSPG,” said Morico.
